chunks.label: How your body feels
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you're sleepy, sick, run-down or itchy, or that something feels good.
chunks.interference: Kimochi warui is both 'gross' and 'I feel sick'; darui (heavy body) gets mixed with nemui (sleepy).

chunks.label: Looks and style
chunks.rationale: Lets you compliment how people look and what they wear.
chunks.interference: Kakkoii is cool, oshare is fashionable; oniai is for couples, niau for clothes.

chunks.label: Tough and tiring
chunks.rationale: Lets you complain that something is a pain, hard, or wearing you out.
chunks.interference: Tsurai, kitsui and shindoi overlap; kurushii leans physical (breathing, too full).

chunks.label: Sad and missing
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you're sad, lonely or nostalgic, or feel sorry for someone.
chunks.interference: Kanashii (sad) vs sabishii (lonely); kawaisou sounds like kawaii but means pity.

chunks.label: Skill and praise
chunks.rationale: Lets you say what you're good or bad at and praise someone.
chunks.interference: Tokui pairs with nigate, heta with jouzu; erai praises effort, yuushuu ability.

chunks.label: Size, look and limits
chunks.rationale: Lets you talk about size and look when choosing things, and set a limit like 'under 1,000 yen'.
chunks.interference: Saizu (clothes and shop sizes) vs ookisa (how big); ika (or less) vs ijou (or more).

chunks.label: Favourites and treats
chunks.rationale: Lets you name a favourite, say 'both', treat yourself and keep a list.
chunks.interference: Dochira mo becomes 'neither' with a negative verb.

chunks.label: Kind and close
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe kind, dependable people and close relationships.
chunks.interference: Naka ii (get along) vs shitashii (close); shinsetsu (kind acts) vs yasashii (kind nature).

chunks.label: Losing and missing out
chunks.rationale: Lets you react to a loss, a near miss, someone else's luck, or your own weakness.
chunks.interference: Kuyashii (gutted at losing) vs oshii (so close) vs nasakenai (pathetic).

chunks.label: Fine, grateful, awkward
chunks.rationale: Lets you say something doesn't bother you, helps you, or feels awkward.
chunks.interference: Heiki vs daijoubu; arigatai describes the help while arigatou is the thanks.

chunks.label: Serious or sloppy
chunks.rationale: Lets you say whether someone takes things seriously or half-heartedly.
chunks.interference: Majime (personality) vs shinken (in the moment); tekitou and iikagen both mean sloppy, iikagen more blaming.

chunks.label: Strict, selfish and mean
chunks.rationale: Lets you complain about strict, selfish, unfair or mean people.
chunks.interference: Zurui (unfair, sly) vs ijiwaru (mean on purpose).

chunks.label: All-in feelings
chunks.rationale: Lets you say you hate something, are hooked on it, can't resist it, or are giving it everything.
chunks.interference: Tamaranai can be praise (irresistible) or complaint (unbearable); hisshi (desperate effort) vs muchuu (absorbed).

chunks.label: Odd, open, quiet
chunks.rationale: Lets you sum up someone's personality in a word.
chunks.interference: Sunao (open, accepting) vs shoujiki (not lying); otonashii is behaviour, shizuka is noise.

chunks.label: Calm and careful
chunks.rationale: Lets you describe how calmly, carefully or eagerly someone works.
chunks.interference: Teinei (careful, polite) vs shinchou (cautious before deciding); shinchou also means height.

chunks.label: Pushy and cocky
chunks.rationale: Lets you complain about people who nag, act superior, overreact or force things.
chunks.interference: Erasou (acts superior) vs namaiki (cheeky junior); shitsukoi (keeps at it) vs gouin (forces it).

drops.reason: Duplicate of めんどくさい (same word, kanji spelling); kept めんどくさい, which ranks higher.
Duplicate of かっこいい (katakana spelling); kept かっこいい, which ranks higher.
